subject: Support macros + escalation path (Marketplace onboarding)
body:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Support macros + escalation path (Marketplace onboarding)

Alex / Elliot — looping you in with Aisha + Olga for security wording.

We’ve had a few repeat patterns from marketplace buyers (AWS + GCP) and we’re losing time to ad hoc responses. I drafted a first pass of support macros + escalation triggers so Support can be consistent and so Eng/Security only gets pulled in when needed.

Attachments:
- Marketplace_Support_Macros_v1.docx (draft macros)
- Marketplace_Escalation_Matrix_v1.xlsx (what to escalate, where, and what info to include)

Macros included (v1):
1) “Marketplace entitlement not found (new subscription)”
   - Ask for: cloud provider (AWS/GCP), marketplace subscription ID / entitlement ID, buyer AWS account ID or GCP billing account, Redwood org name (if any), region
   - Explain: entitlement propagation can take up to ~60 minutes; we can proceed once entitlement sync completes
   - Link: marketplace onboarding troubleshooting doc (Elliot—please confirm final URL)

2) “Provisioning delayed / org not created after subscription”
   - Provide steps to retry from Console marketplace entrypoint
   - Ask for timestamp of subscription + console error code
   - If >60 min, escalate to Eng Platform (ref: ENG-22116 hardening entitlement sync)

3) “Existing Redwood org — how to link marketplace subscription”
   - Explain linking flow + what to do if multiple subscriptions exist
   - Ask for org ID and the email used for marketplace purchase

4) “Billing dimension mismatch / unexpected meter name”
   - Acknowledge and request invoice screenshot + marketplace line item name(s)
   - Provide: we reconcile marketplace dimensions to Redwood usage meters; Support will validate mapping and follow up
   - Escalate to Billing Eng if mismatch is suspected (ref: SUP-4829)

5) “AWS private offer activation timing / limits not updated yet”
   - Set expectations (activation can lag; entitlements may update after offer acceptance)
   - Ask for offer acceptance timestamp and relevant IDs
   - Escalate to Partnerships/Ops only if >1 business day or hard blocker (ref: SUP-4840)

6) “Security packet request (marketplace buyer)”
   - Provide approved public docs links
   - For gated evidence: route via Security/GRC process (Olga—need your preferred language here)

Escalation triggers proposal (high-level):
- P0 (page/urgent): customer cannot provision after >2 hours AND has confirmed subscription IDs; multiple accounts impacted; entitlement sync errors spiking (Support will post in #eng-platform with IDs + timestamps)
- P1 (same-day): single customer blocked >60 min on entitlement/provisioning; repeatable error code; suspected billing dimension mismatch
- Security: any request that implies “security incident,” suspicion of data exposure, or request for non-public SOC2 evidence beyond the approved packet (route to Aisha/Olga; do not ad lib)

Requests:
- Elliot: confirm final docs URLs we should hardcode in macros + any do/don’t wording.
- Alex: confirm the “retry steps” match the current console onboarding entrypoint.
- Aisha/Olga: please redline the security macro language. We want it helpful but tightly scoped.

If we align today/tomorrow, I’ll implement these as Zendesk macros and share with CS/SE for awareness.

Thanks,
Dev
Dev Patel
Support Escalation Owner, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Support macros + escalation path (Marketplace onboarding)

This is great.

Docs URLs:
- We’re planning to land the main page at: /docs/marketplace/onboarding
- Troubleshooting section: /docs/marketplace/onboarding/troubleshooting
- FAQ: /docs/marketplace/faq

Caveat: final redirects are still in flight (internal ticket for redirects), but those should be stable by end of week. I’d avoid hardcoding anything not under /docs/marketplace/*.

Wording suggestions:
- Avoid “we guarantee approval” or “AWS/GCP guarantees timing.” Instead: “Marketplace entitlement propagation is typically quick but can take up to ~60 minutes.”
- For billing: don’t imply a marketplace error; say we’ll “validate the mapping between marketplace line items and Redwood usage meters.”

I can also add a small “What to include in a support ticket” callout on the troubleshooting page if you want.

Elliot

From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwoodinference.com>, Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Dr. Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwoodinference.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 11:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Support macros + escalation path (Marketplace onboarding)

+1. The retry guidance matches what we’re aiming for in the console entrypoint, with one tweak:

In the macro, can we avoid telling users to “create a new org” as a workaround? We’ve seen folks accidentally spin up a second org, which makes the entitlement linking edge-case worse.

Suggested wording for the provisioning delay macro:
- Step 1: Confirm they’re signed into the intended Redwood org (if they already had one)
- Step 2: Visit /console/marketplace (or the marketplace entrypoint) and click “Retry entitlement check”
- Step 3: If they get an error code, ask them to paste it + timestamp

Also, can we add a note that if they subscribed with a different email domain than their existing Redwood org owner, we may need an org admin to complete the link?

Alex

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Wed, Feb 11, 2026 at 2:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Support macros + escalation path (Marketplace onboarding)

For the security macro, here is the language I’d recommend (safe + consistent with our review posture):

- If customer asks “Do you have SOC 2?”
  “Yes. Redwood Inference maintains a SOC 2 Type II report. We can share the report under NDA / via our standard secure evidence process. For marketplace review and general evaluation, please start with our marketplace security overview and data handling documentation here: [links].”

- If customer asks for evidence immediately:
  “We can provide additional compliance evidence upon request through our security team. Please share the requester name, company, and email + any specific control areas they need (e.g., access control, encryption, audit logging, retention). We’ll coordinate secure delivery.”

- Don’t say:
  “We are ISO certified” (unless we’re explicitly stating status/coverage that’s been approved). Also avoid committing to “custom” retention/residency unless it’s already in the published data handling doc.

Escalate to GRC when:
- They request the full SOC2 report, pen test report, or vendor risk questionnaire completion
- They ask for a specific assurance not in the published packet

If you want, we can add a short checklist in the macro for what to collect (company name, requested documents, deadline, buyer’s marketplace provider).

Olga

Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 10:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Support macros + escalation path (Marketplace onboarding)

Approved directionally.

Two additions on escalation triggers:
1) Security escalation (immediate) if a customer reports:
   - suspected unauthorized access to their Redwood org
   - unexpected logins / API key exposure
   - any claim of data leakage

Support should not attempt to investigate beyond collecting basic facts (org ID, timeframe, what they observed) and then route to the security on-call process.

2) For “entitlement not found,” please add an internal-only note:
   - If the customer is within the first 60 minutes after purchase, do not escalate unless there are multiple parallel reports.
   - If >2 hours, escalate with subscription IDs + timestamps. We need that data to correlate with entitlement sync logs.

Otherwise, the macros look good and match the marketplace security claims we can stand behind.

Aisha
Dr. Aisha Rahman
Security Executive Sponsor, Redwood Inference
